ashwin: Heads-up — since last night's rollout I'm seeing a big p99 bump on paged-attn/flash2 for several prod routes. p50 ~= unchanged, p99 jumped from ~42ms -> ~110ms for seq=1024 workloads. Throughput steady. Anyone else seeing this?

katie: Hmm. Which rollout ID? kernel-selector change landed yesterday, could be related.

ashwin: rollout: r-2026-03-16-8143 (deploy-bot shows success). Kernel-selector config updated to prefer flash2 for paged when seq>=512. Logs from one worker attached below (trimmed):

```
2026-03-16T03:12:22Z kernel_select: model=llama-2-13b variant=paged-attn selected=flash2_paged reason=seq_pref batch=32 seq=1024
2026-03-16T03:12:22Z exec: kernel_launch: flash2_paged grid=(256,1,1) sm=sm90 time_ms=0.42
2026-03-16T03:12:22Z mem: kv_page_migrate: pages=3 memcpy_ms=14.6
2026-03-16T03:12:22Z wait: cuda_stream_sync=75.1ms
```

ashwin: The weird part is the large cuda_stream_sync time only showing up on paged+flash2. Non-paged flash2 and paged-flash1 are fine.

leo: I pulled a perf trace from a repro machine. Flame summary: major tail is GPU->CPU synchronization after the kernel, not the kernel itself. Looks like a host-side barrier introduced in the flash2 wrapper when handling migrated pages. Example from perf: 

```
Kernel_flash2_paged       7ms
KV_page_migrate           12ms
Host_sync                 68ms   <-- this is the p99 hit
```

leo: Maybe the wrapper is doing a blocking memcpy+cudaDeviceSynchronize for page faults.

ryan: That matches my local microbench. If you trigger a cold KV page read, flash2 wrapper currently does `cudaMemcpyAsync` then `cudaStreamSynchronize()` to ensure pages are resident before kernel. Old path used pinned staging + overlap. If sync was reintroduced in the selector path, p99 jumps.

ashwin: Good catch. Any quick test we can run on prod-ish infra? I can flip kernel-selector back to prefer flash1 for paged to confirm.

perf-bot: quick perf diff between commits:
```
commit: a1b2c3 -> b4c5d6
route: /chat/long
before(p99): 44.1ms
after(p99): 109.8ms
p50: 9.8ms -> 10.1ms
cpu-side wait: +62.2ms
```

katie: Please do the rollback test, ashwin. If it repros, we can bisect to the exact selector change. Also @ryan can you post the microbench command?

ryan: Sure — run this on a node with similar GPU and model: 

```
./bench_paged_attn --model llama-2-13b --variant paged --kernel flash2 --seq 1024 --batch 32 --cold-kv 1 --iters 200
```
Look at 'host_sync' column in output. Set `--cold-kv 0` to warm the cache.

ashwin: Rolled selector override for staged group -> preferring flash1 for paged. Metrics starting to move back toward baseline over next 5min. p99 currently at 48ms.

deploy-bot: deploy r-2026-03-16-8143-override applied to group staging-2 by ashwin at 1912345720.

leo: If override confirms selector as culprit, bisect plan: start between commit range where selector heuristics were changed. I can run a narrow git bisect across 10 commits. Need a reproducible microbench (ryan's) and a harness that runs the exact kernel selection logic (not a mocked selector).

katie: I'll own the bisect. @leo can you and @ryan give the bench env details (cuda driver, pinned memory flags) so results are stable?

ryan: Driver: 535.54; cuda: 12.1; host OS: ubuntu-22.04. Also check `USE_PINNED_STAGING=1` env — if that was toggled in runtime args, it changes behavior.

leo: Noted. Also add a test that runs with `--kv-warmup` to show warm vs cold delta. If cold causes the extra host_sync we know for sure it's the memcpy+sync path.

ashwin: For the short-term: keep selector override in place and I'll schedule a fix. Long-term: we should drop blocking sync and rely on async migration + kernel read checks or prefetch with pinned buffer.

katie: Sounds good. Assigning follow-ups: ashwin -> keep override + monitor prod; katie -> coordinate postmortem and comms; leo+ryan -> reproduce + bisect and propose patch to avoid sync.

ashwin: I'll post a short incident note once we confirm root cause. Thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: Quick note — if anyone needs the perf trace I uploaded to /mnt/perf/traces/19123456-flash2-paged-sync.svg, ping me.

ashwin: pinged. I'll close the loop here when bisect finishes.
